simple.meaning: שִׁלֵּשׁ (shillêsh) is a Hebrew word meaning “a descendant of the third degree, i.e. great grandchild.” BibleIQ connects the English word back to this source word so its use can be compared across Scripture.
simple.biblicalBackground: שִׁלֵּשׁ (H8029) appears 5 times in the Hebrew Bible, beginning at Genesis 50:23, with occurrences in Genesis, Exodus, Numbers, Deuteronomy.
simple.inThisVerse: In this verse, the tapped English word is source-aligned to שִׁלֵּשׁ (H8029) in the Hebrew text.
simple.whyItMatters: English translations can use the same English word for different Hebrew words. BibleIQ anchors the study in שִׁלֵּשׁ (H8029) before moving outward to related references.
simple.summary: שִׁלֵּשׁ (shillêsh) / H8029 is traced through Genesis 50:23, Exodus 20:5, Exodus 34:7, Numbers 14:18 using source-language evidence and occurrence comparison.

definitions.short: a descendant of the third degree, i.e. great grandchild
definitions.full: H8029. shillesh II. [ שִׁלֵּשׁ ] adjective pertaining to the third ; — only masculine plural as substantive שִׁלֵּשִׁים those of third Generation (grandsons); שׁ ׳בְּנֵי Gen 50:23 (E) sons of those of third Generation , i.e. great-grandsons (see Kö SK 1898, 533 ff. ); עַלשֿׁ ׳עַלבָּֿנִים וְעַלרִֿבֵּעִים Exod 20:5 (E; see [ רִבֵּעַ ]} = Deut 5:9 ; Num 14:18 , compare Exod 34:7 (both J).

occurrences.englishText: Joseph saw Ephraim’s children to the third generation. The children also of Machir, the son of Manasseh, were born on Joseph’s knees.

you shall not bow yourself down to them, nor serve them, for I, Yahweh your God, am a jealous God, visiting the iniquity of the fathers on the children, on the third and on the fourth generation of those who hate me,

keeping loving kindness for thousands, forgiving iniquity and disobedience and sin; and who will by no means clear the guilty, visiting the iniquity of the fathers on the children, and on the children’s children, on the third and on the fourth generation.”

‘Yahweh is slow to anger, and abundant in loving kindness, forgiving iniquity and disobedience; and he will by no means clear the guilty, visiting the iniquity of the fathers on the children, on the third and on the fourth generation.’
